name: The Extra-Owner Anomaly Contradicts the Opposite Wing or Forces Three Pairs
statement: Let an ample two-layer family have overlap $B$ of order at most nine, and suppose each terminal wing has a two-cycle and is either sharp or has the one-unit extra-owner form with disjoint shores of orders two and three. The wings cannot both be sharp. If at least one is extra-owner, then their structures are incompatible or their acquired supports contain three pairwise disjoint direction pairs.
proof: Sharp--sharp is excluded by the overlap lower bound. An extra-owner wing decomposes $G(B)$ into an active path core of order at most two, an ordinary length-three arm, and a rooted four-vertex tree or square. Against a sharp wing, or against another extra-owner decomposition with intrinsic ordinary arm, the arm-recovery theorem makes the same terminal support acquired by both wings but absent from $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$, contradicting the two-layer shadow-intersection identity. The only ambiguity is when two extra-owner decompositions view $B$ as $P_8$ or $P_9$. Reading their consecutive edge directions yields three disjoint acquired supports: $\{x_0,x_2\},\{x_4,x_6\},\{x_3,x_5\}$ on $P_8$, or $\{x_0,x_2\},\{x_5,x_7\},\{x_4,x_6\}$ on $P_9$.
